title: Should We Attend More or Less? Modulating Attention for Fairness
findings: The proposed method, Entropy-based Attention Temperature scaling (EAT), effectively reduces bias (measured as toxicity) in generated text for prompts related to various religious groups. This improvement in fairness for religious groups was achieved by generalizing from a model tuned only to mitigate gender bias, demonstrating the method's ability to apply to multiple forms of social bias.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured bias against religious groups by using the toxicity of generated text continuations from religion-related prompts as a proxy for bias. It also used the pinned AUC equality difference metric for text classification tasks on examples referring to religious subgroups.
